title: The Treasure — Sc122: heads on a string (23-frame bedroom insert)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: The sub-second insert: 23 frames (under one second at 25 fps) that exist only to hold a reaction inside a bigger sequence. Gumball and Darwin hang from a yellow cord at top-bunk height, rendered as blissful floating heads -- eyes closed, mouths cycling through a sung/spoken line, swaying slightly -- while Anais stands on the floor below looking up at them, delighted. The stage is a photographic bedroom plate; the puppets are flat vector. Nothing is chased, built or transformed: the scene teaches how little motion a cut-in needs when the staging (two heads dangling at bunk height, one small witness on the floor) is already the joke.
notes: The background is a real photographic bedroom plate (wooden bunk beds, door, dresser, skateboards) -- the same photo-plate practice as the series' other bedroom scenes; the characters are flat vector puppets over it.
Darwin is the GB211_DARWIN_IN_BOWL_SHOT125 puppet built for the fishbowl shot, reused here a few scenes earlier -- in this shot only his round head reads, hanging at top-bunk height.
Almost nothing moves: across 23 frames the heads sway a few pixels and the mouths cycle, Anais shifts her stance slightly. It is a held insert, not an action beat.
Face comps hold 3210 kf vs 1180 body-puppet kf in the anatomy census -- even in a 23-frame shot, the library's face system outweighs the bodies.
